description: Golden phonetic vocabulary-matcher vectors (issue #283). Generated from hw-phonetic by `cargo test -p hw-core --test phonetic_vectors -- --ignored regenerate`. The `decision` field names which native matcher each unified answer came from: agreed / windows / macos / neither / new.

matcherCases.name: corrects a misrecognized token towards the vocabulary spelling
an empty vocabulary leaves the transcript alone
a vocabulary word of two characters never encodes
a row that carries a replacement is left to the substring path
a whitespace-only vocabulary row is dropped
a token of two characters or fewer is never matched
an exact hit on the FIRST entry is left alone
a newline separates tokens, so a correction on line 2 still lands
matcherCases.was: macOS split on CharacterSet.whitespaces, which EXCLUDES newlines, so every correction after the first line of a multi-line transcript was silently lost. Windows split on all whitespace.

matcherCases.name: a repeated token is corrected everywhere but reported once
matcherCases.was: Windows carried a per-call memo of processed tokens; macOS re-encoded and re-logged every occurrence. The text is identical either way — the \b-anchored pass already rewrote every occurrence on the first hit — so the quieter side wins.

matcherCases.name: a $-token in the vocabulary spelling is inserted literally
matcherCases.was: macOS used NSRegularExpression.escapedTemplate, so every template token was literal. Windows hand-escaped only `$`, leaving $&, $`, $' and ${name} expandable.

matcherCases.name: an exact hit on a LATER entry is protected too
matcherCases.was: Both copies checked the exact hit inside the entry loop and broke out of it, so the guard only fired when the exact entry came first: a token that was already the correct spelling of entry 2 was still rewritten by a phonetic hit on entry 1.

matcherCases.name: an exact hit is protected even when an earlier entry also matches it
matcherCases.was: The same bug, with three entries — the protection has to survive every entry ahead of the exact one, not just the first.

matcherCases.name: the <=2-character gate counts Unicode scalars, not graphemes or UTF-16 units
matcherCases.was: macOS counted graphemes (word.count) and Windows counted UTF-16 code units (word.Length). Two astral characters are 2 scalars, 2 graphemes and 4 UTF-16 units, so Windows let this token through and macOS did not. Scalars is the unit hw-releasenotes pinned, and it is under the gate.

matcherCases.name: a decomposed transcript token equals a precomposed vocabulary word
matcherCases.was: Neither matcher normalized, though VocabularyProcessor.swift:48-54 and VocabularyProcessor.cs:44 both do on the regex path that runs right after, with a comment explaining why. Un-normalized, the decomposed token here does not compare equal to the precomposed vocabulary word, the exact-hit guard misses, the phonetic codes match anyway and the user's own lowercase spelling is rewritten to the vocabulary's capital. NFC first, and it is left alone.

matcherCases.name: case folding has no locale in it
matcherCases.was: Windows added RegexOptions.CultureInvariant with a Turkish-dotless-i comment; macOS used caseInsensitiveCompare with no such note. str::to_lowercase is the Unicode default mapping, which is invariant under every host locale.
